options: A picture or pattern produced by arranging together small colored pieces of hard materials like stone, tile, or glass.
A drawing made using only charcoal and a kneaded eraser.
A large fabric piece created by weaving threads on a wooden loom.
The process of carving complex figures on calabash.
questions.explain: Mosaic is a decorative art technique where small, usually square, pieces of rigid materials (called tesserae) are assembled and glued into a bed of cement or adhesive to form an image.

questions.q: What is the primary difference between a Mosaic and a Collage?
options: Mosaics are only done by machines, while collages are done by hand.
Mosaics use small, uniform, hard pieces laid side-by-side without overlapping, whereas collages use mixed, often flat and overlapping materials like paper and fabric.
Mosaics use wet paints, while collages use dry colors.
There is no difference; the terms mean exactly the same thing.
questions.explain: While both involve pasting materials to a surface, mosaics specifically use hard, non-overlapping materials (tesserae) arranged like a puzzle. Collages embrace overlapping mixed media of varying sizes.

questions.q: When making a durable mosaic on an outdoor wall using stones and broken tiles, which material serves as the best adhesive?
options: Paper gum
Masking tape
Cement or plaster
Cassava starch
questions.explain: Cement or plaster (often called mortar or grout) provides the strong, waterproof grip necessary to hold heavy, rigid materials like stones and tiles permanently on a wall.

questions.q: The small individual pieces of glass, stone, or tile that make up a mosaic artwork are professionally called:
options: Motifs
Tesserae
Stitches
Pixels
questions.explain: In mosaic art, the term 'tesserae' (singular: tessera) is used to refer to the individual small blocks or pieces of solid material used in the composition.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting

questions.q: A common architectural use for mosaics in both ancient and modern times is to:
options: Insulate the roof from heat.
Decorate public floors, swimming pools, and prominent walls.
Provide lighting for dark rooms.
Block sound from entering a building.
questions.explain: Because mosaics are highly durable and water-resistant, they have been historically and modernly used to beautify architectural surfaces like floors, walls, and swimming pools.
